text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P1: post-deploy canary latency spike detected for runtime v3.14. Auto-paged oncall and opened INC-2026-0342.
Jen: I’m on it, looking at canary cluster metrics now. ETA 2m.
Platform SRE: seeing sawtooth on p95 and p99 across canary slice A, CPU on GPU nodes is fine but batch queue depth is oscillating.
Runtime Eng: logs show repeated kernel fallback events after the rollout: 
```
[2026-03-18T12:05:23Z] kernel_selector: falling back to generic_kernel for layer attention.py: kernel_mismatch=1
[2026-03-18T12:05:24Z] batcher: reduced_batch_size for slice A due to queue overfull
```
Kat: batcher windows keep shrinking -> prefetch/backpressure loop. This matches a mis-tuned batching threshold from the release config.
Ryan: Do we have a feature-flag for the new packer that we can kill? If so, flip and route canary back.
Luis: Support reports 6 customer incidents, two with timeouts, one with degraded throughput. Affected customers are on dedicated/d-slices but saw requests routed to canary.
Maya: If this is customer impacting, prepare comms. Status page update once we have mitigation.
Sean: Executing kill-switch now for packer flag on canary slices. Command: `./ffctl set runtime.packer.enabled false --scope canary`
Runtime Eng: saw the flag flip. Initiating traffic re-route off canary to stable model v3.13.
Platform SRE: routing change in progress: canary traffic -> 10% stable, 90% fallback pool. Monitoring p95.
Jen: After reroute, p95 dropped from ~2.8s to ~0.9s on slices handling production traffic. Canary still noisy but no longer serving customer traffic.
incident-bot: INC-2026-0342 updated: mitigation applied (feature-flag kill), customer impact reduced. Pager cleared for now.
Ryan: Recommend rollback of the release artifact and revert batching threshold change from 0.15 -> 0.07 in cookbooks. I’ll open a rollback PR.
Sean: Rollback PR created and tagged for immediate deploy: PR #4719. Initiating controlled rollback to stable.
Runtime Eng: rollback deployed to canary slices at 12:10:45Z. Kernel selector metrics show no further fallback events in the last 2m.
Luis: Support: closed 4 of the 6 tickets as mitigated, two still monitoring while we confirm stability.
Maya: Drafting a short status page note: "We observed elevated latencies after a canary deploy; traffic was routed to stable while we rolled back the change. No ongoing customer impact." Will post when Jen + Ryan OK.
Jen: OK to publish. Logging this for postmortem: root cause likely batching threshold plus an untested packer kernel variant. Follow-ups: 1) add unit/regression test for kernel-selector behavior, 2) add canary-level synthetic load test for batcher, 3) make packer flag default-off behind the rollout gate.
Platform SRE: Handoff to morning oncall for post-deploy follow-up and perf regression monitoring.
Sean: Dropping final commands we ran for runbook: 
```
# disable packer on canary
./ffctl set runtime.packer.enabled false --scope canary
# reroute traffic
./orchestrator route set canary --target stable --percent 100
# rollback artifact
kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deploy/runtime-canary --to-revision=123
```
Jen: Marking this incident resolved for now, will follow up in postmortem doc. Good triage and fast ops. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0342 status: RESOLVED. Postmortem assigned to Runtime Eng and Platform SRE.
